#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproducibly build WSL 2.7.11's Linux-side init on Debian/WSL without the
# unavailable Windows SDK. This reproduces the Linux target, not wslservice.exe.
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

SOURCE=${SOURCE:-/root/src/WSL-2.7.11}
ROOT=${ROOT:-/root/experiments/minimal-wsl/control-plane-build}
LOCALIZATION_HEADER=${LOCALIZATION_HEADER:-$ROOT/Localization.h}
JOBS=${JOBS:-$(nproc)}
BUILD=${BUILD:-$ROOT/native-build}
DOWNLOADS=$ROOT/downloads
DEPS=$ROOT/deps
OUT=$BUILD/out
OBJ=$BUILD/obj

expected_commit=acbcb81fc61079b74835ea7dc2563046b2557033
linuxsdk_version=1.20.0
wsldeps_version=10.0.27820.1000-250318-1700.rs-base2-hyp
linuxsdk_sha=942d36f760446853b29c97f2ee689819bb9305d959342d21df537c1d6981491e
wsldeps_sha=893411830c3bbf58744c44da8d6361018bfee41f22923697b85033aebfc94c7b
gsl_sha=f0e32cb10654fea91ad56bde89170d78cfbf4363ee0b01d8f097de2ba49f6ce9
json_sha=42f6e95cad6ec532fd372391373363b62a14af6d771056dbfc86160e6dfff7aa
localization_sha=374fec04eeff025d2500ff2fcaf61b6f8421debb7d26df3030c24a01feaa8515
feed=https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/shine-oss/13eb32df-d33f-470f-b930-499535a958b4/_packaging/7925a3a1-b93c-4977-8a97-5b877bf2068b/nuget/v3/flat2

fail() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
need() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null || fail "missing command: $1"; }
for command in git curl unzip tar clang clang++ llvm-ar llvm-strip llvm-objcopy sha256sum; do need "$command"; done
[[ $(git -C "$SOURCE" rev-parse HEAD) == "$expected_commit" ]] || fail "source is not pinned WSL 2.7.11"
[[ -z $(git -C "$SOURCE" status --porcelain) ]] || fail "source worktree is dirty"
[[ -f $LOCALIZATION_HEADER ]] || fail "missing generated Localization.h: $LOCALIZATION_HEADER"
printf '%s  %s\n' "$localization_sha" "$LOCALIZATION_HEADER" | sha256sum -c -

mkdir -p "$DOWNLOADS" "$DEPS" "$BUILD"
fetch() {
    local output=$1 url=$2 sha=$3
    if [[ ! -f $DOWNLOADS/$output ]] || ! printf '%s  %s\n' "$sha" "$DOWNLOADS/$output" | sha256sum -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        rm -f "$DOWNLOADS/$output"
        curl -fL -C - --retry 10 --retry-delay 2 --retry-all-errors -o "$DOWNLOADS/$output" "$url"
    fi
    printf '%s  %s\n' "$sha" "$DOWNLOADS/$output" | sha256sum -c -
}
fetch "microsoft.wsl.linuxsdk.$linuxsdk_version.nupkg" \
    "$feed/microsoft.wsl.linuxsdk/$linuxsdk_version/microsoft.wsl.linuxsdk.$linuxsdk_version.nupkg" "$linuxsdk_sha"
fetch "microsoft.wsl.dependencies.amd64fre.$wsldeps_version.nupkg" \
    "$feed/microsoft.wsl.dependencies.amd64fre/$wsldeps_version/microsoft.wsl.dependencies.amd64fre.$wsldeps_version.nupkg" "$wsldeps_sha"
fetch gsl-v4.0.0.tar.gz https://github.com/microsoft/GSL/archive/refs/tags/v4.0.0.tar.gz "$gsl_sha"
fetch json-v3.12.0.tar.xz https://github.com/nlohmann/json/releases/download/v3.12.0/json.tar.xz "$json_sha"

if [[ ! -f $DEPS/.extracted-v1 ]]; then
    rm -rf "$DEPS"
    mkdir -p "$DEPS/linuxsdk" "$DEPS/wsldeps" "$DEPS/gsl" "$DEPS/json"
    unzip -q "$DOWNLOADS/microsoft.wsl.linuxsdk.$linuxsdk_version.nupkg" -d "$DEPS/linuxsdk"
    unzip -q "$DOWNLOADS/microsoft.wsl.dependencies.amd64fre.$wsldeps_version.nupkg" -d "$DEPS/wsldeps"
    tar -xzf "$DOWNLOADS/gsl-v4.0.0.tar.gz" -C "$DEPS/gsl" --strip-components=1
    tar -xJf "$DOWNLOADS/json-v3.12.0.tar.xz" -C "$DEPS/json" --strip-components=1
    touch "$DEPS/.extracted-v1"
fi

rm -rf "$OBJ" "$OUT"
mkdir -p "$OBJ" "$OUT/generated"
cp "$LOCALIZATION_HEADER" "$OUT/generated/Localization.h"

sdk=$DEPS/linuxsdk/x86_64
wsldeps=$DEPS/wsldeps/build/native
common=(
    --gcc-toolchain="$sdk" -fpic -B"$sdk" -isysroot "$sdk"
    -isystem "$sdk/include/c++/v1" -isystem "$sdk/include"
    -isystem "$DEPS/gsl/include" -isystem "$wsldeps/include/lxcore"
    -isystem "$wsldeps/include/schemas"
    -I "$SOURCE/src/linux/inc" -I "$SOURCE/src/linux/mountutil"
    -I "$SOURCE/src/linux/plan9" -I "$SOURCE/src/linux/netlinkutil"
    -I "$SOURCE/src/linux/init" -I "$SOURCE/src/shared/configfile"
    -I "$SOURCE/src/shared/inc" -I "$DEPS/json/include" -I "$OUT/generated"
    --no-standard-libraries -Werror -Wall -Wpointer-arith
    -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -Dswprintf_s=swprintf -fms-extensions
    -target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -D_GNU_SOURCE=1 -D_LARGEFILE64_SOURCE
    -DWSL_PACKAGE_VERSION='"2.7.11.0"' -DWSL_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR=2
    -DWSL_PACKAGE_VERSION_MINOR=7 -DWSL_PACKAGE_VERSION_REVISION=11 -D_AMD64_
    -ffile-prefix-map="$SOURCE"=/usr/src/wsl -ffile-prefix-map="$ROOT"=/usr/src/build
    -g -O2 -DNDEBUG
)

name: transcript-extract
description: Extract minimal plain-text USER/ASSISTANT transcripts from Claude, Gemini, Codex, or Pi Lite JSONL session exports.
---

# Transcript Extract

Use this skill when a user wants a grep-friendly transcript containing only visible conversation turns from one session file. It supports deterministic offline extraction for Claude, Gemini, Codex, and Pi Lite JSONL exports.

## Primary command

```bash
{skillDir}/scripts/transcript-extract --session-file <path>
```

The command prints the transcript to stdout and supports `--output-file <path>`. Replace `{skillDir}` with the installed skill directory supplied by the agent framework.

## Pi session audits

For multi-session usage analysis, use the branch-aware audit command rather
than concatenating session files:

```bash
{skillDir}/scripts/pi-session-audit --sessions-dir ~/.pi/agent/sessions --since 24h
{skillDir}/scripts/pi-session-audit --sessions-dir ~/.pi/agent/sessions \
  --since 2026-08-18T00:00:00Z --until 2026-08-19T00:00:00Z --json
```

Pi branch files repeat their ancestor records. The audit command deduplicates
events and tool calls by stable IDs before reporting totals, tool/helper use,
and failures; it reports raw and duplicate counts so branching overhead remains
visible. Commands that merely mention a `windows-env` helper are not counted as
helper executions.

## Common commands

```bash
{skillDir}/scripts/transcript-extract --session-file ~/.pi/agent/session-transcripts/1784752157.jsonl --mode offline
{skillDir}/scripts/transcript-extract --session-file <path> --source pi
{skillDir}/scripts/transcript-extract --session-file <path> --output-file /tmp/transcript.txt
```

`--mode auto` and `--mode offline` use the same deterministic local adapter. `--mode llm` is rejected with a clear message rather than silently producing an unverifiable result; use the offline adapter for stable extraction.

## Supported formats

- Pi Lite JSONL exports: records with `role: "user"` or `role: "assistant"`, including `session_id`, `cwd`, `timestamp`, and `text`.
- Claude Code JSONL records with `type` and nested `message.role`.
- Gemini JSON/JSONL message records.
- Codex rollout JSONL records with `event_msg` or `response_item` payloads.

The adapter skips malformed lines, tool calls, tool results, reasoning, telemetry, and other event noise. It preserves message text and normalizes timestamps to ISO 8601 where possible.

## Output contract

```text
SESSION_NAME: ...
SESSION_PATH: ...
SESSION_ID: ...
CWD: ...

[2026-07-22T18:28:18.451Z] USER: ...

[2026-07-22T18:48:52.256Z] ASSISTANT: ...
```

`SESSION_ID` and `CWD` are included only when present. `SESSION_NAME` is the recorded session name when available, otherwise a short summary of the first user turn.

## Safety and scope

Use `--mode offline` for repeatable extraction and audit work. Do not send session contents to an LLM unless the user explicitly requests that and has provided an approved workflow. The output intentionally excludes hidden reasoning, tool traffic, and usage metadata.

[2026-08-19T16:55:19.773Z] ASSISTANT: ## Recommended next step

Do **not** do more documentation restructuring. The repository is clean, `main` matches `origin/main`, SQLite integrity is `ok`, and `K-OVERLAY-001` records and hashes match.

### 1. Run the prepared overlay trial

`K-OVERLAY-001` is the next evidence-selected experiment. Before executing:

1. Run the canonical live-state preflight.
2. If `safe:false` because a distro is running, wait—do not stop it automatically.
3. Obtain fresh explicit approval.
4. Run the ordinary **unelevated** harness.
5. Preserve evidence, append trial metadata, synchronize SQLite, update status, and commit/push the result.

### 2. Apply a strict stopping rule

The overlay experiment measures the stock control plane; it does **not** make overlayfs part of Minimal Viable WSL.

After the result:

- **If it reaches B5/B6-T:** use the working stock path as the behavioral oracle for the reduced control plane.
- **If it exposes a narrow requirement belonging to the retained contract:** prepare one evidence-selected candidate.
- **If it demands networking, cgroups, WSLg, system-distro services, or another excluded facility:** stop expanding the stock kernel and pivot to reduced-init work.

### 3. Productive work while awaiting approval/safe state

Map the matching WSL source into the minimum retained path:

```text
VSOCK handshake
→ distro VHDX attachment
→ ext4 mount/root transition
→ command creation
→ stdio and exit-status relay
→ termination/shutdown
```

Identify the exact source files and protocol messages involved, separating them from removable stock policy. This is non-disruptive and is the best parallel task.

So the immediate choice is: **approve the guarded `K-OVERLAY-001` trial when live state is safe, while beginning the source-level control-plane map.**

# Session history

This directory preserves grep-friendly project-session transcripts containing only visible user and assistant messages. Tool calls, tool results, hidden reasoning, credentials, and telemetry are excluded.

Transcripts are historical context, not current instructions or authoritative project state. Verify their claims against `STATUS.md`, Git, SQLite, and immutable trial evidence before acting.

## Sessions

- `2026-08-19_01a01af1-2657-72db-8e7f-422943ba4503.txt` — overlay trial, ETW diagnosis, stock-discovery stopping gate, exact WSL 2.7.12 source map, and reproducible control-plane baseline.

The live Pi JSONL remains in Pi’s session store because moving an active runtime file would break session continuity. The checked-in text file is the durable repository export.
